title: Frequent irregular verbs, infinitives, and commands
prior_teaching_boundary: Only actual reviewed Unit1–5 form, sense and construction milestones count. Earlier infinitive citations are supplied until individually promoted here. Preserve earlier analysis/history and all recognition-only, source-only and reference-only boundaries.
productive_outcomes: Use the complete present/preterite indicative systems of seven selected preterite-present and three anomalous verbs, with their exact changes and bounded elementary uses.
Use the six alternative bēo present-indicative cells with an evidenced ordinary future-state use, retaining the earlier eom/wæs series and avoiding an absolute tense division.
Use complete singular/plural imperative pairs for selected lexical models covering weak I–III, strong I–VII and needed anomalous patterns, including important exceptions and simple negative commands.
Use the selected plain/inflected infinitive pairs in elementary modal/volitional complements and bounded purposive cuman+tō constructions, retaining each lexical government.
Distinguish knowledge of a matter from learned ability, modal sense from morphological tense, and volition from completed action; use new and prior material in meaningful connected practice.
Complete all72 original graded tasks, read the checked controlled dialogue independently, and interpret the exact fisherman excerpt with its explicitly bounded support.
recognition_outcomes: Distinguish actual usable forms from uncertain or unattested modal citation labels; no regular modal imperative or inflected infinitive is invented.
Distinguish taught infinitive morphology from supplied availability, relative, content and participial constructions in the source.
Distinguish selected course forms from valid documented alternatives and unassigned additional lexical rows.
bounded_scope: First/second personal genitives remain recognition-only; agreeing possessives are separate productive lemmas.
Instrumental forms, plural ān and eall remain recognition/reference; *sǣwa remains a supplied starred reconstruction without milestones.
Nabban, bregdan and fēolan remain at prior recognition scope; their presence in a prior table does not authorize productive new commands.
Diagnostic īecan, gierwan, ęfnan and hycgan lack arbitrary productive argument frames; use isolated form exercises unless a frame is expressly audited.
Hātan active indicative morphology does not teach hātte, infinitival causatives or double-accusative naming.
Beodan offer and lǣtan let do not automatically license command/causative complement frames; biddan ask needs an explicit new construction if used with an infinitive.
Prior source-only temporal/connective ðā, nū, ęft, swā, sōðlice, destination tō, motion on, mid and relative/content/purpose clauses remain supplied unless explicitly newly taught.
Simple ne negation extends only to newly audited systems; no negative copula, negative concord or every contracted negative form follows.
Participles, passive, subjunctive/optative wishes and unsupported subordinate moods remain supplied/deferred. Creation wishes must not be labelled imperative morphology.
No ge- or other prefix generalization; new prefixed lexemes need their own evidence.
I.4.18 and the birds candidate remain Unit7 deferrals; no earlier active or archived artifact is rewritten.
Only43 imperative-model lemma systems (44 rows with alternate bēon) and two additional infinitive-only skill verbs receive these new nonfinite/imperative milestones.
Finite indicative roster is ten complete12-cell systems plus alternate bēon6; no new modal imperative or defective modal infinitive is fabricated.
Existing plain-infinitive citation IDs are promoted only after same-lemma/same-surface/morphology identity checks; their old analysis and supplied/per-chapter histories remain explicit.
The new thing-matters sense is distinct from earlier thing-1; prior noun forms remain unchanged.
No numbered Cook set is assigned; existing79 assigned/565 deferred items, I.4.18 and birds deferments persist.

The source-local habban plus tō-inflected infinitive availability construction remains supplied as a whole, together with its clauses. The coordinator explicitly overrides the grammar audit’s new_recognition recommendation; no general recognition milestone or unaided recall target is added.

Ordinary intransitive cuman is explicitly new production in u06-cuman-intransitive. Earlier finite morphology did not teach this construction; it is required both in the connected account and before the selected same-subject purpose construction.
The grammar audit’s postposed-pronoun imperative variant is reference evidence only. Assigned commands omit the subject or use a preposed subject; no extra plural -e recall milestone is assigned.

audited_inflection_rules.claim: Selected preterite-presents have present 1sg=3sg, a special 2sg, and one plural stem/form for all persons; their past is weak. Learn each selected present/past pair as a complete indicative system.
Where Cook prints the past in -e followed by etc., the 2sg adds -st and the plural changes -e to -on. These are declared model-derived cells, not separately quoted textual tokens.
Don, gan, and willan have complete selected present/preterite indicative systems. Gan uses eode for the past; willan has wille in both present 1sg and 3sg, not an automatically added ordinary -ð.
The six beo/bist/bið/beoð indicative person cells supplement the prior wesan system and share its prior past; future or habitual/gnomic state depends on context.
audited_inflection_rules.boundary: Productive use is explicitly contextualized expected-later state; no new tense of every verb or future auxiliary willan is inferred.

audited_inflection_rules.claim: Second singular commands address one person; second plural commands address more than one. The subject may be omitted or stated.
audited_inflection_rules.boundary: Only selected second-person systems are assigned. First/third-person optative commands remain later scope.

audited_inflection_rules.claim: Ordinary strong singular imperative is the present stem without the infinitive ending; the second plural normally matches the present indicative plural. Present 2sg/3sg mutation is not mechanically imported into the command stem.

Contracted strong verbs restore final h in the singular command: wrīh, tēoh, seoh, sleah, fōh. The vowel qualities/quantities are lexical class patterns; seoh/sleah are short, wrīh/tēoh/fōh retain the selected long vowel. Their plurals remain contracted.

Heavy weak-I singular commands lack final -e; short/geminate-j patterns retain -e and lose the j-induced gemination in the singular: nęre/nęriað, fręme/fręmmað, sęle/sęllað, sęte/sęttað. Gierwan has giere/gierwað.
Selected heavy weak-I cys and gefyl simplify the final double consonant; plurals cyssað and gefyllað retain it. This is distinct from the short-stem -e model and from settan, whose singular is sete.
audited_inflection_rules.boundary: Final simplification is frequent and the selected normalized model; do not assert that all unsimplified final spellings are impossible.

audited_inflection_rules.claim: Strong j-presents use weak-I-like -e singular commands: bide, site, lige, hęfe, sciepe, swęre; plurals retain their selected present stems. Hebban/hęfe and licgan/lige require their own consonant alternations.
Weak-II singular command changes -ian to -a; plural retains -iað: lufa/lufiað.
The selected complete weak-III pairs are hafa/habbað, leofa/libbað, saga/sęcgað, hoga/hycgað. Cook also gives sęge for saga and lifiað beside libbað, with optional e in sęcg(e)að/hycg(e)að.
audited_inflection_rules.boundary: Variants are documented reference alternatives, not automatic extra recall targets; nabban remains unassigned here.

audited_inflection_rules.claim: Don has dō/dōð, gan gā/gāð; wesan/bēon gives wes/wesað and bēo/bēoð. No positive willan command pair or modal command pair is invented.
Cook notes shortened plural -e before an immediately following subject pronoun: binde gē, not bindað gē. This positional command variant is distinguished from indicative inversion.
audited_inflection_rules.boundary: Assigned commands omit the subject or use a preposed subject. No unrestricted plural -e production target, and no first/third-person command system.

audited_inflection_rules.claim: An earlier supplied dictionary citation does not constitute learned infinitive syntax. Only explicitly selected plain-infinitive cells are promoted; exact prior IDs may be retained with old analysis and history preserved.
audited_inflection_rules.boundary: Four defective modal headwords remain citation labels, with no infinitive/inflected target. Unselected earlier lexical rows get no milestone.

audited_inflection_rules.claim: For selected -an infinitives the course chooses -anne after tō; -ian therefore gives -ianne and geminated stems remain geminated. Contracted final -n gives -nne: fōnne, sēonne, dōnne, gānne, bēonne. The preposition tō is a separate token.
audited_inflection_rules.boundary: -enne is a documented valid variant; selected -anne is not a universal grammatical requirement or a license to derive unattested modal cells.

audited_inflection_rules.claim: A finite selected modal/volitional verb takes a plain infinitive in the bounded same-subject construction; the finite verb marks person/number and present/past, while the infinitive does not agree.
audited_inflection_rules.boundary: These lexical senses differ. Do not treat every modal as English must, or replace actual indicative past by an automatically hypothetical would/could reading.

audited_inflection_rules.claim: Selected cuman + tō + inflected infinitive expresses the purpose of the same subject’s coming. Cook also documents bare infinitives with motion/specification/purpose.
audited_inflection_rules.boundary: No claim that all purposes require tō; a valid bare-purpose alternative can miss the stated target without being ungrammatical. General accusative-and-infinitive and dependent-subject syntax remain outside scope.

audited_inflection_rules.claim: Ordinary ne before a second-person imperative gives a negative command.
audited_inflection_rules.boundary: Construction only; the evidence does not teach ondrǣdan, its reflexive/genitive frame, or a nyllan imperative system.

audited_inflection_rules.claim: Source-local habban + tō-inflected infinitive describes something held/available for the named action.
audited_inflection_rules.boundary: Not a general rule translating all habban+tō as modern have to obligation, nor an assigned passive-infinitive system.

audit_recommendation_precedence: Audit recommendations are evidence inputs. The explicit lexical and grammar inventories below control assigned teaching scope; in particular source-local availability remains supplied, not an independent recognition outcome.

grammar_audit_boundaries.claim: Infinitive-looking headwords are unattested citation labels, supported by Fulk§123 and partly flagged by Cook125. No inflected infinitive or imperative generated.
No positive imperative assigned. Cook139 supplies only negative plural nellað/nyllað; do not invent singular will or pair will/willað.

Cook §126/§198 and Wright §540 call wite (and Wright witaþ) imperative. Fulk §123 says preterite-presents have no formal imperative and use subjunctive substitutes. No regular modal imperative system is generated or assigned here; documented command substitutes are not denied.
grammar_audit_boundaries.status: resolved: documented functional commands, deliberately unassigned

grammar_audit_boundaries.claim: No imperative in Cook130–131 or Fulk123; no complete imperative pair proposed. Attested uninflected citations do not license unattested modal imperative reconstruction.

global_rules: The chosen form inventory governs independent recall; complete unselected audit rows do not become learner reference tables or milestones.
Every introduced conjugational pattern has complete selected command/infinitive cells, with rules and ordinary uses together.

Accompanying present participle cweðende, with ðus; no finite ending or command.
Each source prepositional phrase supplied locally; neither familiar headword nor motion makes its government previously taught.

Nim and gā are direct second-singular imperatives. No PP imperative extension.
Tō + inflected infinitive morphology; source availability frame supplied separately.
Sealde with accusative gift and dative recipient; source nouns supplied.

support_groups.local_meaning: Then, as soon as the fisherman saw that the young man was lying at his feet.
support_groups.scope_note: Supply the whole temporal frame and embedded content clause, with geonga/fiscere/fōtum/æt. His feet contextually refers to the fisherman. Familiar finite indicatives do not make either subordinate construction taught.
Supply mid mildheortnesse as manner and the prefixed verb ūpāhōf. Hē is the fisherman; hine is Apollonius.

support_groups.local_meaning: And led him with him to his house.
support_groups.scope_note: Supply mid him accompaniment and tō his hūse destination. Hine is Apollonius; him and his contextually refer to the fisherman. Hūs is not in the active prior lexicon and must be supplied.

support_groups.local_meaning: And set before him the provisions that he had to offer him.
support_groups.scope_note: Supply ēstas, lęgde, dative him beforan, object-relative ðe, and the available-to-offer habban construction. Tō bēodanne morphology is new Unit6, offer sense prior, but the object/recipient availability frame remains supplied. The second him is Apollonius, not a reflexive recipient.

support_groups.local_meaning: He still wanted, according to his ability, to show him greater kindness.
support_groups.scope_note: Wolde + plain infinitive volition is new Unit6. Supply gīet, be his mihte, ārfæstnesse, and gecȳðan with accusative thing shown/dative recipient. Mihte here is a noun. No fact about prefix ge- or generalized government is inferred.

support_groups.local_meaning: He then tore his cloak in two.
support_groups.scope_note: Supply tōslāt, wǣfels and the entire on twā expression. The subject remains the fisherman; no new subordinate clause. Do not test the gender of an unexpressed noun or infer a general on+motion rule.
Prior giving frame; supply Apollonie, healfan dǣl. One half renders ðone healfan dǣl without inventing a second object.
Supply cweðende as a present participle accompanying the same subject, plus ðus. It is not a finite past or a command. No productive participial syntax is introduced.

support_groups.local_meaning: Take what I have to give you.

new_compositions.title: Food and water for the journey
new_compositions.text: Se mann cwæð: ‘Ic wille faran. Mīn scip is gearu. Cumað and helpað mē.’ Twēgen gefēran cōmon tō helpanne. Se mann cwæð: ‘Nimað ðone męte and berað hine. Giefað ðǣm fuglum ðæt wæter.’ Se gefēra cwæð: ‘Ic mæg ðone męte beran. Wē sculon ðæt weorc gefręmman.’ Ðā gefēran bǣron ðone męte and gēafon ðǣm fuglum ðæt wæter. Se mann cwæð: ‘Sittað and etað.’ Ðā gefēran ǣton. Hīe fōron.
new_compositions.intended_meaning: The man said: ‘I want to travel. My ship is ready. Come and help me.’ Two companions came to help. The man said: ‘Take the food and carry it. Give the birds the water.’ The companion said: ‘I can carry the food. We must perform the work.’ The companions carried the food and gave the birds the water. The man said: ‘Sit and eat.’ The companions ate. They travelled.
new_compositions.reference_limit: Se gefēra identifies a contextual member of the two companions without naming which. Final hīe does not uniquely encode whether the man accompanies them. The food being eaten is a contextual inference; its object is unexpressed.

grammar_inventory.description: Use the bēo-series present indicative for an explicitly expected later state with a taught nominative predicate.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Future state is the productive use selected here. Documented habitual/gnomic uses are background, not an automatic new productive construction; bēo-series forms must not invariably be translated as future.

grammar_inventory.description: Simple preverbal ne extends to the selected noncontracted durran and magan indicative clauses.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: No negative concord, new negative copula, or unassigned nillan/nytan/nabban production.

grammar_inventory.description: The finite modal/volitional verb carries subject agreement; its selected plain infinitive does not acquire person/number endings or tō in the taught construction.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Only the expressly selected forms, senses and constructions are assigned.

grammar_inventory.description: Elementary purpose after cuman is expressed with tō plus the selected inflected infinitive; the understood actor is the person/people who come.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: No general purpose-clause subjunctive, indirect command, arbitrary controller or other infinitival construction.

grammar_inventory.description: The selected infinitives retain their audited lexical argument relations: carrying/taking/eating have accusative objects, helping a dative person, and giving an accusative thing with dative recipient.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Only the expressly selected forms, senses and constructions are assigned.

grammar_inventory.description: Second-singular commands address one person; plural commands address two or more, without a separate dual ending. The subject can remain unexpressed in the selected direct instructions.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: These are second-person commands, not third-person optative wishes or a new general politeness system.

grammar_inventory.description: Ne directly precedes the selected negative imperative in the taught prohibition.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: No general claim that every Old English prohibition must have imperative morphology.

grammar_inventory.description: The prior cweðan direct-quotation frame now also introduces the independently taught second-person commands. Quoted reference belongs to the speaker/addressee context.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Only the expressly selected forms, senses and constructions are assigned.

grammar_inventory.description: Faran means go/travel in an ordinary intransitive clause and as the action in the newly taught volitional complement.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: No destination, vehicle, motion-preposition or sailing sense is implied.

grammar_inventory.description: Cuman means come in an ordinary intransitive clause and supplies the movement verb before the selected same-subject purpose infinitive.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: No unassigned destination phrase or sense of becuman follows.

grammar_inventory.description: Gān is used in the selected ordinary objectless go clauses, modal complements and direct commands.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Source intō and other destination phrases remain supplied unless separately assigned.

grammar_inventory.description: Dōn means do/perform with an accusative work/thing in the selected elementary clauses, complements and commands.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: No causative, passive, perfect or arbitrary phrasal sense.

U03-ADJ-USE.evidence_note: Strong/weak conditions and agreement. Cook says weak sometimes after possessives; this is not a universal possessive→weak rule.

U03-STRONG.evidence_note: Complete strong pattern, short/long stems, æ/a alternation, disyllabic syncope and optional loss of -u, -e stems, h-loss and consonant simplification.

U03-WEAK.evidence_note: Complete weak pattern. Selected ordinary Gpl -ra; -a/-ena are explicitly admitted alternatives. Comparative Gpl contraction is explained, not a license to invent arbitrary assimilation.

U03-COMPARE.evidence_note: Regular, umlaut and irregular degrees; comparative weak, superlative usually weak. Selected representative series below, not blanket mastery of all examples.

U03-ADVERB.evidence_note: Adverb formation and degree; wīd→wīde, swīð→swīðe very, sōð→sōðlice truly. Adverbs modify verbs, adjectives or adverbs.

U03-NUMERAL.evidence_note: Cardinal/ordinal spellings and complete one/two/three rules; ordinals weak except ōðer.

U03-POSSESSIVE.evidence_note: Six agreeing first/second-person possessives; third-person genitives indeclinable. sīn not selected.

U03-DEMONSTRATIVE.evidence_note: Full that/this paradigms. Cook prints short-e ðes, not ðēs; selected double-s variants. Instrumental is reference recognition only.

U03-WRIGHT-USE.evidence_note: Positive/superlative predicate strong; eall and ōðer always strong. Full paradigms confirm agreement; mixed-gender predicate exception remains outside present tasks.

U03-WRIGHT-SYNCOPE.evidence_note: Long-disyllable syncope with retention before consonantal endings; analogical micles/miclum explicitly printed; hāligu and hālgu variants; -erra/-erre may simplify.

U03-WRIGHT-E.evidence_note: Full wilde pattern used by ūre, with its separate fem.Nsg exception in §464.

U03-WRIGHT-GEARU.evidence_note: Complete gearu strong pattern (gearone, gearore, gearora; gearw- before vowel) and weak gearwa/gearwe.

U03-WRIGHT-HEAH.evidence_note: Complete contracted hēah strong pattern and weak hēa, hēan. Selected hēanne/hēarre/hēarra/hēaum; source also gives simpler variants.

U03-WRIGHT-COMPARE.evidence_note: Comparatives weak; irregular series and their variants. Does not individually attest every derived case.

U03-WRIGHT-NUMERAL.evidence_note: Plural ān rare with different distributive sense, not cardinal one with plural count nouns; 4–19 generally uninflected before a noun, with separately conditioned inflection outside this unit.

U03-WRIGHT-POSSESSIVE.evidence_note: uncer/incer/ēower explicitly like hālig; ūre like wilde except F.Nsg ūre. ūrre/ūrra may simplify. Combined with §§429/431 yields transparent pattern-derived cells.

U03-WRIGHT-ADVERB.evidence_note: Exact wel/bet/betst and regular -or/-ost pattern; Cook hook spelling selected for bęt/bętst.

U03-THAN.evidence_note: Attested Beowulf469 comparison Sē wæs betere þonne iċ! provides a nominative standard after than with unexpressed repeated copula. Bounded analogous composition, not a claim that all than-constructions take nominative.

authoring_rules: Retain all72 exact task prompts and stable task/key IDs; no numbered Cook set is assigned.
Display all120 new complete irregular indicative cells and the six bēo cells, with earlier eom/wæs reference clearly distinguished. Every person/number must be recoverable.
Display complete selected imperative and infinitive pairs with rules, stem changes, lexical exceptions and declared variant choices. Extra audit rows remain unassigned evidence.
Unattested/uncertain modal infinitive labels are not usable forms or commands. Do not generate regular tables for defective systems or invent a separate bēo past.
Teach only the checked elementary lexical frames. Morphology-only diagnostic models receive no unrecorded government, content clauses, general motion rule or auxiliary system.
Earlier citation-form promotions preserve stable IDs and histories. Supplied Bēon optative, participles, earlier recognition-only systems and *sǣwa retain their distinct records and limits.
Retain the checked68-word account and ten examples, labelled new teaching material. Record any additional Old English dependencies before inserting prose.
Retain the76-word original excerpt, ten supports and three original notes. Declare the added final quotation mark and the excerpt boundary; distinguish source words from editorial context.
Keep the availability-infinitive phrases, free relative and other source-only syntax supplied. The noun mihte is not the modal; hæbbe is not uniquely mood-diagnosed from its spelling.

Prepare the separate key from actual Old English with models, targets, essential meaning, explanations, alternatives and diagnoses. Contextual reference and intended modal sense do not eliminate linguistically valid alternatives.
Independent reviewer solves all actual learner tasks before opening the key or private answer/translation witnesses, retains frozen solutions, and edits only review files.

Resolve material findings before complete LuaLaTeX exports, full content parity and every-page visual inspection. Preserve earlier records in reviewed register integration, export Beads and save local revisions. Do not draft Unit7.

lexical_frame_evidence.scope_note: Finite forms, infinitive identity, lexical sense, and government are separate dependencies. New compositions require all of them; these frame records are evidence recommendations, with assignments controlled by the coordinator’s contract.

frames.construction: know an accusative nominal fact or matter
frames.prior_boundary: New lexical use; a prior paradigm/citation alone did not establish this construction.
frames.exclusions: No finite content clauses; thing in the fact/matter sense is explicitly new, not silently inherited from physical things.
frames.evidence_relation: Declared bounded teaching generalization from the cited page-image evidence; not a claim that a new lesson example occurs verbatim in the source.

frames.construction: know how to / be able through learned skill + plain infinitive of the same subject
frames.prior_boundary: New lexical use; a prior paradigm/citation alone did not establish this construction.
frames.exclusions: No nominal acquaintance/knowledge frame or hypothetical conditional syntax.
frames.evidence_relation: Declared bounded teaching generalization from the cited page-image evidence; not a claim that a new lesson example occurs verbatim in the source.

frames.construction: be able / have the capacity to + plain infinitive of the same subject
frames.prior_boundary: New lexical use; a prior paradigm/citation alone did not establish this construction.
frames.exclusions: No epistemic possibility or permission requirement; no actual infinitive magan/mugan assigned.
frames.evidence_relation: Declared bounded teaching generalization from the cited page-image evidence; not a claim that a new lesson example occurs verbatim in the source.

frames.construction: need to + plain infinitive of the same subject
frames.prior_boundary: New lexical use; a prior paradigm/citation alone did not establish this construction.
frames.exclusions: No genitive/accusative noun-object government is inferred from this infinitival frame.
frames.evidence_relation: Declared bounded teaching generalization from the cited page-image evidence; not a claim that a new lesson example occurs verbatim in the source.

frames.construction: dare to + plain infinitive of the same subject
frames.prior_boundary: New lexical use; a prior paradigm/citation alone did not establish this construction.
frames.exclusions: No modal infinitive or imperative derived from the citation label.
frames.evidence_relation: Declared bounded teaching generalization from the cited page-image evidence; not a claim that a new lesson example occurs verbatim in the source.

frames.construction: must / be obliged to + plain infinitive of the same subject; preterite actual past obligation
frames.prior_boundary: New lexical use; a prior paradigm/citation alone did not establish this construction.
frames.exclusions: No debt construction, predictive future, reported-command clause, or automatically conditional should.
frames.evidence_relation: Declared bounded teaching generalization from the cited page-image evidence; not a claim that a new lesson example occurs verbatim in the source.

frames.construction: may / be allowed to + plain infinitive; preterite was/were allowed to in explicit permission context
frames.prior_boundary: New lexical use; a prior paradigm/citation alone did not establish this construction.
frames.exclusions: The separate obligation sense is documented in the source but not assigned by this frame. No defective modal infinitive target.
frames.evidence_relation: Declared bounded teaching generalization from the cited page-image evidence; not a claim that a new lesson example occurs verbatim in the source.

frames.construction: wish / want / intend to + plain infinitive; preterite actual wanted/intended
frames.prior_boundary: New lexical use; a prior paradigm/citation alone did not establish this construction.
frames.exclusions: Not an automatic future auxiliary or hypothetical would; no positive command system.
frames.evidence_relation: Declared bounded teaching generalization from the cited page-image evidence; not a claim that a new lesson example occurs verbatim in the source.

frames.construction: do/perform an accusative action, deed, or task
frames.prior_boundary: New lexical use; a prior paradigm/citation alone did not establish this construction.
frames.exclusions: No causative do, put/placement, or idiomatic particle construction.
frames.evidence_relation: Declared bounded teaching generalization from the cited page-image evidence; not a claim that a new lesson example occurs verbatim in the source.

frames.construction: ordinary go/walk, with no obligatory object
frames.prior_boundary: New lexical use; a prior paradigm/citation alone did not establish this construction.
frames.exclusions: No universal goal-preposition rule; source goal phrase can remain locally supplied.
frames.evidence_relation: Declared bounded teaching generalization from the cited page-image evidence; not a claim that a new lesson example occurs verbatim in the source.

frames.construction: ordinary come, including the motion verb in the selected purpose construction
frames.prior_boundary: New lexical use; a prior paradigm/citation alone did not establish this construction.
frames.exclusions: No added accusative motion object or generalized goal-preposition syntax.
frames.evidence_relation: Declared bounded teaching generalization from the cited page-image evidence; not a claim that a new lesson example occurs verbatim in the source.

frames.construction: ordinary go/travel with no obligatory complement; may occur as willan’s plain infinitive
frames.prior_boundary: New lexical use; a prior paradigm/citation alone did not establish this construction.
frames.exclusions: No new goal preposition, route object, or figurative fate sense.
frames.evidence_relation: Declared bounded teaching generalization from the cited page-image evidence; not a claim that a new lesson example occurs verbatim in the source.

frames.construction: alternate bēon series with ordinary predicate adjective/state, in explicitly expected-later context
frames.prior_boundary: Copular predicate agreement and ordinary present/past wesan were prior; new bēon forms and their contextual future-state use are explicit additions.
frames.exclusions: No passive/perfect auxiliary use. Generic/habitual function is described; a bare bið is not always future.
frames.evidence_relation: Declared bounded teaching generalization from the cited page-image evidence; not a claim that a new lesson example occurs verbatim in the source.

frames.construction: cuman + tō + inflected infinitive expressing why the same subject comes
frames.prior_boundary: New lexical use; a prior paradigm/citation alone did not establish this construction.
frames.exclusions: No general rule forbidding bare infinitival purpose; no infinitive with an independently expressed subject.
frames.evidence_relation: Declared bounded teaching generalization from the cited page-image evidence; not a claim that a new lesson example occurs verbatim in the source.

frames.construction: source-local have/hold something available for the action, with tō + inflected infinitive
frames.prior_boundary: Habban ordinary possession is prior; this source-local relation is explicitly new recognition.
frames.exclusions: No general modern have to obligation, no independent production of the source’s relative syntax.
frames.evidence_relation: Declared bounded teaching generalization from the cited page-image evidence; not a claim that a new lesson example occurs verbatim in the source.

frames.construction: second-person imperative command, subject omitted or stated before the selected full form
frames.prior_boundary: New lexical use; a prior paradigm/citation alone did not establish this construction.
frames.exclusions: No first/third-person optative commands; complete forms do not imply every lexical use is already taught.
frames.evidence_relation: Declared bounded teaching generalization from the cited page-image evidence; not a claim that a new lesson example occurs verbatim in the source.

frames.prior_boundary: New lexical use; a prior paradigm/citation alone did not establish this construction.
frames.exclusions: No extra ondrǣdan government or nyllan paradigm from the evidence.
frames.evidence_relation: Declared bounded teaching generalization from the cited page-image evidence; not a claim that a new lesson example occurs verbatim in the source.

frames.construction: direct quotation may contain an imperative command
frames.prior_boundary: Direct-quotation reporting frame is prior; the newly licensed content here is a direct imperative command. The source itself uses the separately supplied reporting participle cweðende.
frames.exclusions: No indirect-command infinitive or dependent optative syntax.
frames.evidence_relation: Declared bounded teaching generalization from the cited page-image evidence; not a claim that a new lesson example occurs verbatim in the source.
